subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Sample Roasting: Testing Before Committing
description: A short lesson to help you apply Sample Roasting: Testing Before Committing.

hook.text: Before roasting a full batch, roasters test small samples (50–150 grams) to evaluate the green coffee's potential.

buildup.text: Sample roasters are tiny drum machines that produce consistent, standardized light roasts for cupping (professional tasting).

discovery.text: Cupping the sample reveals acidity, sweetness, body, and defects—information that guides the production roast profile.

twist.text: A coffee that cups brilliantly as a sample can still fail in production if the profile isn't translated well.

climax.text: The gap between sample and production roasting is where many roasters struggle. Scaling up isn't just multiplying numbers.

punchline.text: Small test, big decision. Every production batch starts as a 100-gram trial.

quiz.question: Why do roasters use sample roasting before production?
options: To evaluate the green coffee's potential and guide the production roast profile

details.summary: Sample roasting uses small batches of 50 to 150 grams to evaluate a green coffee before committing to a full production roast. Roasters follow a standardized light profile to reveal the bean's inherent qualities without the influence of heavy roast development.
details.whyItMatters: Sample roasting is the coffee buyer's essential evaluation tool. It reveals defects, flavor potential, and quality before large purchasing decisions are made.
takeaways: Sample roasts use tiny batches of 50 to 150 grams
A standardized light profile reveals inherent bean quality
Results guide purchasing and production roast profile decisions

faq.question: How does a sample roast differ from a production roast profile?
faq.answer: Sample roasts follow a standard fast light profile designed to highlight a green coffee's defects and potential, not to optimize flavor for drinking. Production roasts are then customized based on sample roast findings.

faq.question: What equipment is typically used for sample roasting coffee?
faq.answer: Dedicated sample roasters like the Ikawa or Probatino handle small batches with precise temperature control. They are much smaller and faster than production roasters, designed for quick evaluation cycles.
